content.prompt: The sector graphs show information about different coloured cars in two car parks.

spec.description: Car park B, with internal labels Red, Blue, Black, White and Other clockwise from the top. Red is largest and slightly less than half; Black is smallest and its white label is diagonally rotated.
spec.mathematics: Reconstruction uses approximate visual shares 44%, 17%, 6%, 10%, 23% solely to reproduce the source appearance. No exact proportions are inferred for calculations.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Marty says: “There are more red cars in car park B than in car park A.”
Explain why he might not be correct.

answer.short: The graphs show proportions, not actual numbers. Car park A may contain many more cars than car park B.
answer.worked:
$$\text{Number of red cars}=\text{red share}\times\text{total cars}$$
Car park B has the larger red share, but the totals are unknown. Car park A could contain enough more cars to have more red cars.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What other information do you need to be able to confirm whether Marty is correct?

answer.short: The total number of cars in each car park.
answer.worked:
Use the total number of cars in each car park with its red share:
$$\text{Number of red cars}=\text{red share}\times\text{total cars}$$
Compare the two results. Exact counts also require sufficiently precise red proportions.
